answer: A strong defence is an escalating per-identity rate limit. Every agent gets a small free quota of actions per epoch, enough for honest work. Beyond it, each extra action costs a fee that doubles, like a marble rolling faster down a slope: the tenth extra action costs far more than the first. A sybil farm running a thousand fake names must pay that curve on every name, so its cost grows while honest agents, signing each real job with a quill, stay inside the free quota. The walnut-hard shell is the math itself: volume is what attackers need, and volume is exactly what the curve prices out.
